mechanism_claims.claim_text: MP-C, cMP-C and tMP-C were tested for Staphylococcus aureus membrane permeabilization using SYTOX Green; cMP-C showed rapid permeabilization at the tested MIC multiple, while MP-C and tMP-C increased mainly at higher MIC multiples.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: MP-C, cMP-C, tMP-C against Staphylococcus aureus
mechanism_claims.limitations: Assay supports membrane permeabilization phenotype in S. aureus, not a precise molecular binding target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The peptides inhibited biofilm formation and eradicated established biofilm only at measured MBIC/MBEC concentrations; this is a phenotypic antibiofilm activity record, not a direct mechanism claim.
mechanism_claims.entity_scope: MP-C, cMP-C, tMP-C against S. aureus and P. aeruginosa biofilms
mechanism_claims.limitations: Crystal-violet MBIC/MBEC values do not identify a biofilm molecular target.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: cMP-C was designed with terminal cysteines and oxidized to a looped/disulfide-constrained analogue; CD and serum-stability evidence support structure/stability context but not a separate antimicrobial target.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Structural and stability assays explain analogue design and cautions; they are not endpoint activity rows.

mechanism_claims.claim_text: The paper hypothesizes that cMP-C may be trapped in bacterial cell wall or biofilm after cell-surface aggregation, requiring higher concentration to reach the cell membrane.
mechanism_claims.limitations: Author-framed hypothesis; keep out of direct_mechanism class.
